name: MMStar
description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples. Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline, then human review is applied to ensure each curated sample exhibits visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requires advanced multi-modal capabilities.
creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
citeAs: Chen, L., Li, J., Dong, X., Zhang, P., Zang, Y., Chen, Z., Duan, H., Wang, J., Qiao, Y., Lin, D., & Zhao, F. (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330v2 [cs.CV].
rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from current multi-modal benchmarks (SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU) using an automated pipeline with LLM inspectors to filter out visually unnecessary or leaked samples. Then, three human experts conducted a manual review to ensure visual dependency, coverage of capability dimensions, and requirement of advanced multi-modal abilities. The pipeline narrowed down from 22,401 samples to 11,607 candidate samples, and finally 1,500 high-quality samples were selected.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples were collected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: SEED-Image, AI2D-Test, ScienceQA-Test, MMBench-EN-Dev, MathVista-Mini, and MMMU-Val.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples were split into four difficulty categories based on hit counts of 16 LVLMs: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11 hits), hard (4-7 hits), and tough (0-3 hits). Samples with hit counts of two or fewer from LLM inspectors were retained after coarse filtering.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied using two closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro) and six open-source LLMs (sized 20B or larger) as inspectors with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy. Samples answerable by more than 2 of the 8 LLM inspectors were excluded. This reduced the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 samples. Subsequently, manual review by three experts further filtered to 1,500 final samples, ensuring visual dependency, capability dimension coverage, and difficulty diversity. All questions were converted into multiple-choice format.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three human experts conducted manual review of the coarsely filtered samples to ensure: (1) each sample's answer should be based on understanding of visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. Samples were also categorized into four difficulty levels (easy, moderate, hard, tough) based on LVLM hit counts.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Difficulty levels were determined by tallying hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples. LLM inspectors' hit frequency was used to assess visual dependency and data leakage risk. Samples with hit counts of two or fewer (approximately 75% of LLM inspectors failing) were retained.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three domain experts conducted the manual review; no further demographic details are provided.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs used as automated inspectors: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro (closed-source), LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B (open-source). VLMEvalKit was used as the evaluation codebase.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMStar addresses critical issues in LVLM evaluation by ensuring visual dependency and minimizing data leakage, which helps provide fairer and more accurate assessments of multi-modal AI capabilities. This can guide the research community toward more reliable benchmarking and development of LVLMs, reducing misjudgments of actual multi-modal gains.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is constructed from existing benchmarks which may carry their own biases. The source distribution is skewed toward SEED (28.3% of final 1,500 samples), MMBench (24.4%), and MathVista (23.0%), with smaller proportions from AI2D (13.1%), MMMU (6.7%), and ScienceQA (4.6%).
rai:dataLimitations: MMStar is currently a static benchmark of 1,500 samples, which may eventually be subject to data leakage as models are trained on more data over time. The benchmark focuses on multiple-choice format questions. The authors acknowledge the need to expand to a larger, online test set with dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample integrity.
rai:dataUseCases: MMStar is designed for Testing and Evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). It is used to assess multi-modal capabilities across 6 core dimensions and 18 detailed axes. It also supports computation of two novel metrics: multi-modal gain (MG) and multi-modal leakage (ML), to measure actual performance gains and data leakage from multi-modal training.
